key_insight: PoM (Polynomial Mixer) is a learned polynomial token-mixing module that compacts tokens into a small polynomial-based summary and lets each token retrieve context from that summary, achieving attention-like contextualization in linear time. It also satisfies a provable contextual mapping property, preserving the transformer's universality as a sequence-to-sequence approximator.
problem_solved: Replaces quadratic-cost self-attention with a linear-time token-mixing mechanism that retains expressive power while lowering compute and memory for long sequences.
method: Learn a polynomial function that aggregates input tokens into a compact representation (polynomial summary) rather than computing pairwise attention.
Provide a retrieval operation where each token extracts contextual information from the learned polynomial summary to update its representation.
Design PoM as a drop-in module for transformer layers, yielding O(N) complexity instead of O(N^2) for sequence length N while proving the contextual mapping (universality) property.
impact: Enables transformers to scale to much longer sequences with substantially reduced compute and memory overhead while preserving theoretical expressivity, making it practical for resource-constrained and large-context applications.
visual_elements: Architecture flow diagram: tokens -> learned polynomial aggregation -> compact summary -> per-token retrieval -> updated tokens (shows single-pass linear pipeline).
Complexity chart: bar/curve comparing O(N^2) attention vs O(N) PoM across increasing sequence lengths (compute & memory axes).
Schematic of the polynomial aggregator: illustrate coefficients/learned bases compressing multiple tokens into a small set of polynomial features.
Mini example: small sequence walkthrough showing how one token retrieves context from the polynomial summary (before/after embeddings).
paper_title: PoM: A Linear-Time Replacement for Attention with the Polynomial Mixer
paper_authors: David Picard, Nicolas Dufour, Lucas Degeorge, Arijit Ghosh, Davide Allegro
